description: Source-informed first reproduction candidate; unpublished distributions are assumptions, not fitted to model scores.

paper_fixed: 64 x 64 x 64 reciprocal-space grid; three shape and three phase families
Actual occupied-voxel bounding-box oversampling exceeds two on all axes
Artificial object phase spans 2pi-5pi inside support before reciprocal-origin recentering
Poisson intensity counts; official log1p/min-max input and reciprocal-phase target
source_informed: Isotropic Gaussian convolution on [-1,1]^3 follows the earlier Patching_DL random_noise formula, including same-mode zero-boundary convolution
The random field is interpolated in the same rotated particle frame as analytic phases
replication_assumptions: All unspecified intervals are uniform; photon count is log-uniform. These values were fixed before running the official model.
Gaussian centers and sigmas use particle half-extent units; cosine cycles use the uncut cube diameter. Component signs, weights and directions follow the existing simulator.
Earlier-source correlation length 0.01-0.1 is a normalized kernel sigma, not a confirmed final training distribution. correlation_length_voxels is used only by legacy_filter.
Oversampling 2.2-4.0, broad Gaussian sigma 0.35-0.85, cosine 0.25-1.25 cycles, and peak counts 1e5-1e6 are first-pass assumptions.
Continuous half-space shapes are voxelized with unit amplitude. No atomic lattice, LAMMPS relaxation, amplitude noise or diffraction blur is introduced.
Centered NumPy FFT is discrete kinematic scattering, not the unpublished atomic PyNX generator.
Integer periodic reciprocal shifts preserve the Fourier pair; the matching real-space phase ramp is applied to clean truth. Both phase spans and wrapped edge-energy fractions are recorded.
Each sample is an independently generated particle; no particle is reused across calibration and evaluation.
